newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa declines comment on UK sale report.
newsitem.headline: Axa declines comment on UK sale report.

text.p: French insurance group Axa, which recently combined with rival UAP, declined to comment on Monday on a British newspaper report it would rationalise its holdings by selling off one of its British insurers.
"We never comment on rumours," said a group spokesman.
The report in The Times said the insurer would sell Equity and Law, a UK insurance firm in an auction which could raise up to one billion stg -- double the 467 million price paid by AXA in 1987.

The Times added that AXA-UAP also holds a 60 percent stake in the UK Sun Life Group which includes the general insurer, Provincial. A sell-off of that stake was cited as another possibility in the report, which did not name any sources.
Demand for British insurers is seen as high, with a race already under way to take over the mutual insurer Scottish Amicable which has seen five suitors come forward.
